pr.title: coverage: Store coverage source regions as `Span` until codegen
pr.description:
Historically, coverage spans were converted into line/column coordinates during the MIR instrumentation pass.

This PR moves that conversion step into codegen, so that coverage spans spend most of their time stored as `Span` instead.

In addition to being conceptually nicer, this also reduces the size of coverage mappings in MIR, because `Span` is smaller than 4x u32.

---

There should be no changes to coverage output.
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: PR #133418 is an explicit semantics-preserving refactor/optimization, not a bug fix. The old `make_source_region` in `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coverage/mod.rs` and the new `make_coverage_span` in `compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/src/coverageinfo/mapgen/spans.rs` contain identical logic: `ensure_non_empty_span` (same body-span bound, same adjacent `{`/`}` checks), byte-based `line_and_byte_column`, the same doctest line offset, and identical `check_source_region`/`check_coverage_span` validation (nonzero coordinates, unset end_col high bit, ordered region). The only change is *when* the same conversion runs: MIR now stores the raw `Span` and codegen converts it, skipping a mapping when conversion returns `None` (old code's `filter_map` did the same skipping at instrumentation). Thus the final set of emitted coverage regions is the same for every input; only the MIR-dump representation differs (`start:col - end:col` vs raw `Span` debug syntax, e.g. `14:9 - 14:10` vs `14:10: 14:10`). The task and frozen analysis explicitly warn that changed MIR dump coordinates/zero-width spans are not a coverage-output regression, so there is no source-grounded "wrong transformation" whose concrete observable value can differ from the original. Constructing a pair that differs would require an arbitrary representational or return-value change not justified by the PR (e.g., returning raw span offsets instead of line/column regions), which the instructions forbid. Therefore no valid original/transformed counterexample exists.

analysis.originalLogic: Historically, the InstrumentCoverage pass converted each coverage mapping's source span into a `SourceRegion` (start_line, start_col, end_line, end_col) during MIR instrumentation. `create_mappings` took `tcx`/`ExtractedHirInfo`, looked up the body's `SourceFile`, and called `make_source_region`, which first ran `ensure_non_empty_span` (expanding an empty span to an adjacent `{` or `}` within the body span) and then `check_source_region` (rejecting zero coordinates, a set high bit in `end_col`, or an improperly ordered region). The resulting `Mapping` stored `source_region`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The pre-optimization transformation was to eagerly convert `Span` to line/column `SourceRegion` inside InstrumentCoverage and store that in `Mapping`. This PR defers conversion to codegen (`coverageinfo/mapgen/spans.rs::make_coverage_span`) and stores the raw `Span` in `Mapping` instead. This is an optimization/refactor, not a confirmed bug fix: the patch says "There should be no changes to coverage output." It reduces the size of coverage mappings in MIR because "`Span` is smaller than 4x u32."
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions compiled with coverage instrumentation (`-C instrument-coverage`), including mappings for ordinary code, branches, MCDCBranch/MCDCDecision; empty spans such as closing braces; spans at body-span boundaries; doctests and macro-expanded code; multiple source files per CGU; and MIR dumps at InstrumentCoverage and after CleanupPostBorrowck.
analysis.summary: Coverage span conversion was moved from the InstrumentCoverage MIR pass into LLVM codegen. MIR now stores raw `Span`s in coverage `Mapping`s instead of eagerly computed `SourceRegion` line/column pairs, reducing MIR mapping size. The old eager conversion and its validation (empty-span expansion, nonzero/ordered coordinate checks, reserved `end_col` high bit, byte-based columns, doctest line offsets) were preserved but relocated to `make_coverage_span`. MIR dumps therefore show raw `Span` debug syntax and can show zero-width spans that are expanded only later in codegen; final coverage output is intended to be unchanged.
analysis.trigger: InstrumentCoverage builds coverage mappings for a function and, under the old logic, immediately converts every Code/Branch/MCDCBranch/MCDCDecision mapping's span into a `SourceRegion`; the new logic keeps the `Span` in MIR until codegen's coverage map generation.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled and mappings are being created for a function.
All BCBs with spans have been assigned coverage counters; `term_for_bcb` expects this.
A function's coverage mappings are assumed to be in the same source file as its body span.
The source map can look up the body span's source file and relative positions.
LLVM requires 1-based nonzero coordinates, an unset high bit in `end_col`, and ordered regions (start <= end).
Empty spans may need expansion to an adjacent brace, but only within the function's body span.
pitfalls: Do not treat changed MIR dump coordinates as a coverage-output regression: with stored `Span`s, dumps print raw span syntax, and empty spans may appear zero-width until codegen expands them. For example the old dump had `14:9 - 14:10`, while the new dump prints `14:10: 14:10`; the PR states coverage output should not change.
Column numbers must be byte-based, not character-based, because `llvm-cov` expects byte columns.
`end_col`'s high bit is reserved by LLVM to mark gap regions, so it must remain unset.
Improperly ordered regions (end < start) or zero coordinates must be skipped, otherwise `llvm-cov` exits with a fatal error.
Empty-span expansion must stay within the body span and only look at adjacent `{` or `}`; otherwise return `None` and skip the mapping.
Doctest line offsets must still be applied during conversion; there is no supported column offset.
The CGU file table is keyed by `StableSourceFileId` and sorted by filename then stable id; function mappings are still assumed to share the body span's file.
A used function with no embedded mapping data is now skipped with a debug message rather than triggering the old `bug!` assertion.
analysis.testStrategy: Use focused MIR-dump tests under `tests/mir-opt/coverage/` at both `InstrumentCoverage` and `CleanupPostBorrowck` stages to verify that `coverage ... =>` lines now print `Span` debug form (for example `$DIR/instrument_coverage.rs:14:10: 14:10 (#0)`) rather than `start_line:start_col - end_line:end_col`. Include functions with mappings on closing braces/empty spans, branch and match-arm mappings, nested functions, and doctest/macro cases, so span expansion and validation are exercised at codegen rather than instrumentation. Separately compare end-to-end coverage output before and after the transformation, since the historical expectation is "There should be no changes to coverage output." Do not infer from MIR coordinate differences alone that the replacement transformation is incorrect; the decoded diff shows the same source program with raw spans at MIR level and deferred expansion in codegen.
